# 3 Maccabees Chapter 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** Ptolemy Struck Down and Then Persecutes

---

**2:1** He had hardly finished his prayer when the high priest Shimon was struck with awe and with trembling, and he said to him: O Ptolemy, this great God who looks down from on high and watches over all things has not made this place holy for the sake of the wicked or for those who seek to enter it lawlessly.

**2:2** And he has struck down the former Heliodorus, who came with a full army to plunder the temple treasury, and driven him away shamefully.

**2:3** And now too, seeing you as one who has transgressed against the laws, he will not leave you unpunished.

**2:4** He had hardly finished these words when Ptolemy was gripped by a great terror, and he was stricken on all his members and his strength was drained from him.

**2:5** His companions saw him fall down, and hastily carried him out, seized as he was with great terror.

**2:6** So when God had thus exercised his judgment, he was no longer able to accomplish any of the things he had threatened.

**2:7** He returned to Egypt, filled with bitterness of heart, but God had delivered the people from harm.

**2:8** But when Ptolemy had returned to Egypt and had increased in viciousness, being aided in this by the drinking companions he had around him who had no sense of justice, he was not satisfied with his previous wicked deeds.

**2:9** He uttered threats against the Jews, and having written a letter he commanded his forces to have the Jews all imprisoned, wherever each was to be found.

**2:10** When the letter was dispatched, it said: King Ptolemy Philopator to the generals and soldiers in Egypt and all its territories, greetings.

**2:11** I am well, as are my affairs.

**2:12** Since our expedition to Asia has turned out as we wished, and we returned safely, we have decided — not through the use of force but through goodwill and much generosity — to bestow benefits on the inhabitants of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.

**2:13** For the Jews in those places, however, having made us joyfully welcome and greeted us earnestly, followed us to where we were going and showed themselves favorably disposed toward us in all sorts of ways.

**2:14** But many of those Jews are found to be troublemakers and do not submit to our rule, and they act with contempt toward our sacred sanctuaries.

**2:15** Therefore, being led by kindness rather than by harshness of spirit, we have decided that they be registered along with us.

**2:16** They are to be enrolled in a census and to be assigned to particular service in our household, and all those registered in this census are to be branded with an ivy-leaf, the emblem of Dionysus, and reduced to their former inferior status.

**2:17** Those who do not choose to participate in this reduced status will be taken away and disciplined; those who refuse with contempt will be put to death.

**2:18** Our purpose in all this is to make them all equal in status, and to have them abandon their foreign and barbaric customs.

**2:19** Those who betray the Jews or hand them over to us will be rewarded with the property of the one betrayed.

**2:20** When this decree was read out in Egypt, it caused great sorrow everywhere.

**2:21** The Jews mourned deeply and wept, for their hearts were in bitter anguish.

**2:22** Everywhere they made lamentation and filled the streets with weeping and lamentations.

**2:23** Those who were of gentle spirit also wept for those more lowly and unfortunate than themselves.

**2:24** There was great distress in every house, and the sighing and lamentations did not stop.

**2:25** Grief filled all of Egypt, and there were none who were not moved by the plight of the Jews.
